question: If tan θ = x - (1)/(4x), then sec θ - tan θ is equal to:
solution:
**Given:**

tanθ = x - (1)/(4x)

**Formula used:**

sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ 

**Calculation:**

sec2θ = 1 + tan2θ 

⇒ sec²θ = 1 + (x – 1/4x)²

⇒ sec²θ = 1 + x² + 1/16x² – 2 × x × 1/4x

⇒ sec²θ = 1 + x² + 1/16x² – 1/2

⇒ sec²θ = (1 – 1/2) + x² + 1/16x²

⇒ sec²θ = (2 – 1)/2 + x² + 1/16x²

⇒ sec²θ = 1/2 + x² + 1/16x²

⇒ sec²θ = (x + 1/4x)²

⇒ secθ = (x + 1/4x) or -(x + 1/4x)

Now,

sec θ – tan θ

On taking secθ = (x + 1/4x) 

⇒ x + 1/4x – (x – 1/4x)

⇒ (x + 1/4x – x + 1/4x)

⇒ (1/4x + 1/4x)

⇒ 2/4x

⇒ 1/2x

Again,

On taking secθ = -(x + 1/4x)

⇒ -(x – 1/4x) – (x – 1/4x)

⇒ -x – 1/4x – x + 1/4x

⇒ (-x – x)

⇒ -2x

**∴ The required value is - 2x or (1)/(2x)**​​
